text: Move items or fluid between two machines without a line of pipes. Snap a relay plate onto a face of the sending machine, aim it at the receiving face with a Lattice Tuner, and every second the cargo jumps across.
Relays are for distance. Two Tribal Power blocks that touch can trade through their faces instead (see [How stations work](echo_workshops)); a vanilla chest still needs a hopper or a plate.
pages.title: Wireless cargo
Snapping and aiming
text: Right-click a plate onto a face of a machine or chest. Holding a plate, a plain click places it, even on a machine that opens a screen. It pulls from the block it is stuck to.

The plate pulls through the face it sits on and delivers into the face you marked, and both follow that block's face settings: the plate's face must give (**Output** or **Both**) and the marked face must take (**Input** or **Both**). A station's sides start as **Input** and only its bottom as **Output**, so set the face first.
A [Stone Font](stone_font) is set for plates already: its top and bottom faces are **Both**, so item and fluid plates work there either way.
Aim it with the **Lattice Tuner**: right-click the face that should receive the goods, then right-click the plate. The plate sends everything it pulls to that face.

Keep Pulse within 8 blocks of the plate, and a Resonance Totem of its voice there too, awake or dim but not quiet: **Air** for Item, Fluid and Longreach relays, the **Loom** for Astral ones. A Kinship Totem lending that voice counts as well. Without it the plate waits. A server can drop this rule with **automationNeedsVoices** in the common config.

steps.caption: Snap an Item Relay onto the top of the sending chest.
Right-click the top of the far chest with a Lattice Tuner to mark it.
Then right-click the plate with the tuner. It now sends to the marked face.
Stand an Air Resonance Totem within 8 blocks of the plate: relays carry on the Air voice.
Pulse near the sending plate, and up to 16 items a second cross over.

pages.title: Items or fluid
text: Each second a relay moves up to **16 items** or **250 mB**.
Item and Fluid relays carry what their name says. A **Water Seal** in the **Rune** slot makes any plate carry fluid; an **Earth Seal** makes it carry items.

A **Fire Seal** in the **Rune** slot makes a **void plate**: it burns what it pulls from its machine instead of sending it anywhere, items on an Item Relay, fluid on a Fluid Relay. It only burns what its filter names, so an empty filter burns nothing. A void plate burns by tab 1's filter.

Plates start as a **Blacklist**, so a fresh void plate with cobblestone marked burns everything except cobblestone. Switch it to **Whitelist** first to burn only what you mark, or leave it a Blacklist and mark what to keep.
A void plate still needs Pulse and its voice. Each beat it burns up to **16 items** or **250 mB**, more when ranked, and pays the plate's usual Pulse for it.
For fluid, park a Spirit Cistern at each end. Relays move fluid; they do not store it.

pages.title: The filter
text: Open a plate to fill its **Filter**: eight slots that hold a picture of an item, never the item itself. Click a slot with something in hand to mark it, with an empty hand to clear it, or shift-click goods in your inventory.

The button beside it switches the list. A **Blacklist** holds the marked goods back and lets everything else cross; an empty blacklist, the way a plate starts, sends everything. A **Whitelist** sends only the marked goods.
For fluid, mark a bucket or any filled container: a water bucket lists water.
Crouch and right-click a plate with an empty hand to switch its list without opening it.

pages.title: Channels
text: A plain plate sends to one place. Rank it and it opens more **channels**: [Echo Attune](machine_ranks) opens a second, Bind a third, Manifest a fourth. Each channel has its own destination and its own filter.

Pick a channel with the numbered tabs at the top of the plate, then right-click the plate with a marked Lattice Tuner to aim that channel. **Unlink** forgets a channel's destination and keeps its filter.

**Priority** sends goods to the first channel, in number order, that takes them and has room: whitelist ores on channel 1 to a furnace, and let channel 2 take everything else to storage. **Round-robin** has the channels take turns.
The channels share the plate's one transfer a beat, so a ranked plate moves as much as before, just to more places.

pages.title: Three distances
text: - **Item** and **Fluid Relays** reach **32 blocks**, and each beat that moves something costs **8 Pulse**.
- **Longreach** relays reach **128 blocks**, for **16 Pulse** a beat.
- **Astral** relays have no distance limit and cross between worlds, for **32 Pulse** a beat.
A beat that moves nothing costs nothing.

Ranked plates (see [Machine ranks](machine_ranks)) pay **118%**, **143%** or **182%** of that and move as much more: about **19 / 23 / 29** items or **294 / 357 / 455 mB**. Pulse per item stays about even.

pages.title: The Lattice Tuner
text: Right-click the face of the block you want goods delivered to; the tuner remembers that face. Then right-click the plate with the tuner to aim it. Mark the destination, never the plate. A plain right-click marks any block, even a cache or chest that opens on a click.
The mark stays on the tuner after you aim, so one mark can aim several plates; right-click another block to replace it. A mark on the block the plate itself sits on is refused.
The distance limits above apply.
Aiming survives picking the plate up, and so does its filter. Breaking a plate drops its Rune beside it.
A plate is yours: only you and your [camp](shared_camps) can open it, change its filter, or aim it with a tuner.

pages.title: Controls and when it waits
text: A steady redstone signal pauses a plate. Power the tuner's target block to stop a transfer from the far end.
A lever on a Tribal Power station, cache or cistern also stops plates pulling from it or delivering into it.
A comparator on a plate reads **0** unlinked, **1** linked but waiting, **15** while moving cargo.

Both ends must already be loaded. An unloaded or full destination makes the relay wait; only a Fire Seal plate destroys anything. Relays never load chunks themselves, so put a Wayanchor at the far end if it must work while you are away.
Crouch and right-click a plate with this book to see its link, cost and why it is waiting.
